subtopics.title: VAT — the Tax Already Inside the Price

questions.question: A camping gas stove is quoted at R840,00 EXCLUDING VAT. Its VAT-inclusive price is:
A till slip total of R1 069,50 INCLUDES VAT. The amount before VAT is found by:
options: Multiplying R1 069,50 by 0,85 to get R909,08
Dividing R1 069,50 by 1,15 to get R930,00
Multiplying R1 069,50 by 1,15 to get R1 229,93

questions.question: The standard-rated part of the basket costs R138,00 including VAT. The VAT contained in it is:
Which set of items is ZERO-RATED, so that no VAT is charged on them?

subtopics.title: Discount — What Comes Off, and Off What

questions.question: A jacket marked R780,00 is reduced by 25%. The sale price is:
15% off the R780,00 jacket, followed by a further 10% off at the till, gives a final price of:
Why is '15% off then 10% off' NOT the same as 25% off?
options: Because VAT is recalculated between the two discounts
Because the second discount is taken off the already-reduced R663,00, not off the marked R780,00, so the combined multiplier is 0,765 — a 23,5% discount
Because the shop rounds each discount to the nearest rand
Because two discounts may never be used together

questions.question: 'Buy two, get one free' is equivalent to a discount of about:
options: 33,3%, because you pay for two of the three items
25%, because you get a quarter more
66,7%, because two of three are paid for

subtopics.title: Simple Interest — Growth in a Straight Line

questions.question: R6 000 is invested at 6,5% SIMPLE interest per year for 4 years. The interest earned is:
In a simple-interest calculation, nine months must be substituted as:
What makes interest 'simple' rather than compound?
options: It is paid only on small amounts
It uses a lower rate than compound interest
It is calculated on the original amount every period, never on interest already earned
It is only available for less than a year

questions.question: R6 000 grows to R6 660,00 in 2 years under simple interest. The annual rate is:

subtopics.title: The Washing-Machine Decision — Three Tools, One Answer

questions.question: A washing machine marked R6 800,00 is on sale at 20% off. The sale price is:
Six months' simple interest on R5 900 at 5% per year is:
Waiting six months instead of buying on sale leaves the family:
options: Better off by R147,50, because interest was earned
Exactly even, because the effects cancel
R1 360,00 worse off, with no other effect
R1 212,50 worse off overall, and R752,50 short of the R6 800 marked price

questions.question: Which set of habits is named as the mark-earning routine for this topic?
options: Write the substitution, keep units and cents, round only at the end, and answer in a sentence
Round every step to the nearest rand as you go
Work only in percentages and convert at the end
Estimate first and skip the working if the estimate looks right

subtopics.title: The Till Slip at the Corner Shop

questions.question: When the shelf price of washing powder reads R62,50, that R62,50 is:
options: The price before VAT is added at the till
The price with VAT already included

questions.question: The whole basket totals R386,00 with R248,00 of it zero-rated. The VAT on the slip is:
The 'sugar stirred into tea' comparison makes which point about VAT?
options: VAT is only charged on groceries
VAT must be paid separately at the till
VAT rates change with the seasons
VAT is already folded into the price, so you cannot find it by taking 15% of the full amount

subtopics.title: The Sale Sign That Says More Than It Gives

questions.question: If 25% comes off a price, the quickest single step is to multiply by:
Compared with a true 25% discount on R780,00, the '15% then 10%' sale costs the shopper:
The plain-language rule for chained percentages given in the lesson is:
options: The second percentage only eats what the first one left on the plate
Add the percentages, then take the average
Always apply the smaller percentage first
Chained percentages must be converted to fractions

questions.question: The price after 15% then 10% off R780,00 is R596,70. To recover the marked price you would:

subtopics.title: Money That Grows the Same Amount Every Year

questions.question: R6 000 at 6,5% simple interest pays the saver, in each of the four years:
options: R390,00 every year — the same amount each time
A growing amount: R390,00, then R415,35, then R442,35

questions.question: The closing balance after four years is:
Substituting 9 instead of 0,75 for nine months would make the interest answer:
Why is buying the washing machine on sale better than waiting six months for interest?
options: Because interest is taxed and discounts are not
Because 5% is a smaller number than 20%
Because R1 360 of discount is far larger than R147,50 of interest — a net gain of R1 212,50 in actual rands
